title: Integrative AI-assisted modeling suggests CPPF binding at a composite [Formula: see text]/[Formula: see text]-tubulin interface pocket dominated by [Formula: see text]-tubulin contacts.
authors: Yang, Jixin; Liang, Lisha; Zhu, Dengchao; Yin, Xuzhe; Feng, Yizhuo; Tang, Shaojun; Li, Muzi
one_liner_zh: 该文利用Protenix、RFAA、Umol等AI结构预测工具和MD模拟，研究抗癌药物CPPF与微管蛋白α/β异二聚体的结合模式，属于蛋白质-配体相互作用的结构计算建模，方法创新且直接命中蛋白质结构计算课题。
abstract: Microtubules are dynamic cytoskeletal polymers assembled from alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimers. Microtubules are validated targets for novel therapeutic drugs, yet therapeutic efficacy targeting them is often compromised by multidrug resistance (MDR). 5-(3-chlorophenyl)-N-(3-pyridinyl)-2-furamide (CPPF) is a novel microtubule-targeting anticancer agent which was found to disrupt microtubule growth in cells and inhibit tubulin polymerization in vitro. CPPF could suppress the growth of multidrug-resistant cell lines and demonstrate anti-tumor efficacy in animal models. However, the fundamental mechanism of how CPPF disrupts microtubule assembly remains unclear. To investigate this, we performed structure prediction using Protenix, RoseTTAFold All-Atom (RFAA) and Umol, as well as molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, using the human alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimer (PDB ID: 5IJ0) for analyzing the interaction between CPPF and tubulin. Our results showed that CPPF binds at the alpha/beta interface with dominant contributions from beta-tubulin residues, particularly VAL236 and LEU253. In isolated-monomer comparisons, beta-tubulin exhibited more favorable binding energetics and deeper, broader free-energy minima than alpha-tubulin. Supplementary simulations on the alternative beta-tubulin conformational state (PDB: 6E7B; straight microtubule-lattice) indicated that CPPF binding is preserved across the two major beta-tubulin conformations, with comparable MM-PBSA binding free energies. Taken together, these findings establish a plausible binding mode for CPPF at the alpha/beta-tubulin interface, providing a structural hypothesis for understanding its anticancer potential against multidrug-resistant cancers. Experimental validation through binding assays or crystallography is warranted to further substantiate these computational insights.
abstract_zh: 微管是由α/β-微管蛋白异二聚体组装而成的动态细胞骨架聚合物。微管是新型治疗药物的有效靶点，然而针对其的治疗效果常因多药耐药性（MDR）而受损。5-(3-氯苯基)-N-(3-吡啶基)-2-呋喃甲酰胺（CPPF）是一种新型微管靶向抗癌剂，被发现能在细胞中破坏微管生长，并在体外抑制微管蛋白聚合。CPPF能抑制多药耐药细胞系的生长，并在动物模型中显示出抗肿瘤功效。然而，CPPF如何破坏微管组装的基本机制仍不清楚。为探究此问题，我们使用Protenix、RoseTTAFold All-Atom (RFAA)和Umol进行结构预测，并采用分子动力学（MD）模拟，利用人α/β-微管蛋白异二聚体（PDB ID: 5IJ0）分析CPPF与微管蛋白之间的相互作用。结果表明，CPPF结合于α/β界面，主要贡献来自β-微管蛋白残基，特别是VAL236和LEU253。在分离单体比较中，β-微管蛋白表现出比α-微管蛋白更有利的结合能量学特征，以及更深、更宽的自由能最小值。对替代β-微管蛋白构象状态（PDB: 6E7B；直微管晶格）的补充模拟表明，CPPF结合在两种主要β-微管蛋白构象中均得以保留，且MM-PBSA结合自由能相当。综合来看，这些发现为CPPF在α/β-微管蛋白界面的结合模式提供了合理依据，为理解其针对多药耐药癌症的抗癌潜力提供了结构假说。通过结合实验或晶体学进行实验验证，对于进一步证实这些计算见解是必要的。
